prompt: 2,4-pentanedione (acac) has pKa ~9 — dramatically more acidic than acetone (pKa ~20). Why?

options.label: The α-H sits between two C=O groups, so the enolate is stabilized by resonance onto BOTH oxygens.
The additional C=O inductively withdraws electron density, polarizing the α-C-H bond.
The sp² α-carbon formed on deprotonation is more stable here due to the planar geometry of acac.
The deprotonated enolate is aromatic (6 π electrons in a planar 5-atom system).

explanation: Only in a 1,3-dicarbonyl is the α-H flanked by two C=O. Deprotonation gives an enolate where the negative charge delocalizes onto EITHER oxygen (not just one) → doubly stabilized, hence ~11 pKa units more acidic than a mono-carbonyl. The anion isn't aromatic — it just has two excellent resonance stabilizers.
